title: Need and signal
question: What changed, and who is affected?
description: Capture a user, client, operational, market, or organizational signal without immediately treating a requested feature as the only solution.

title: Discovery and framing
question: Which problem is worth solving now?
description: Study users, context, feasibility, constraints, risks, and strategic fit, then define an outcome and the uncertainty that must be reduced.

title: Direction and prioritization
question: What will we invest in, defer, or reject?
description: Compare opportunities, appetite, capacity, dependencies, risk, and expected value to make an explicit investment and sequencing decision.

title: Experience and solution design
question: How might the complete experience and system work?
description: Explore interaction, content, service, architecture, data, security, and operational options before selecting a coherent approach.

title: Delivery planning
question: How will we deliver safely in useful slices?
description: Break the intended outcome into integrated increments, clarify dependencies and quality conditions, and choose a suitable planning and flow method.

title: Build and integrate
question: Can the team create a working, maintainable increment?
description: Implement interface, service, data, and infrastructure changes collaboratively while integrating frequently and keeping quality feedback close to development.

title: Verify and assess risk
question: Is the change fit for use and safe to release?
description: Test important functional, accessibility, security, performance, data, and operational risks against agreed evidence rather than only checking happy paths.

title: Deploy and release
question: How will the capability reach users safely?
description: Deploy repeatable artifacts, migrate data where necessary, control exposure, communicate changes, and retain rollback and incident readiness.

title: Operate, learn, and improve
question: What happened in real use, and what changes next?
description: Observe technical and user outcomes, respond to incidents and support needs, compare results with the intended outcome, and improve product and system.
